title: Direct image preserves constructible towers
statement:
Work in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix primes $p\ne\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; more generally the assertion holds for a separated finite-type $k$-morphism with all geometric fibres of dimension at most $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Fix a compactification $f=\bar f\circ j$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. On the derived categories of the coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], put
$$Rf_{!,\bullet}=R\bar f_{*,\bullet}\circ j_{!,\bullet}:D^+(\operatorname{Tow}(X,\mathcal O_E))\longrightarrow D^+(\operatorname{Tow}(Y,\mathcal O_E)),$$
where $j_{!,\bullet}$ is levelwise extension by zero. With the levelwise identification of [sk-lem-sp-tower-levels], equivalently clause (1) of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels], one has
$$(Rf_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet)_n\simeq Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}C_n.$$
If $C_\bullet\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], then $Rf_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$. Here finite-level $\Dctf$ and Tor amplitude have the meaning of [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. No normalization of the input tower is required.

proof.text: By [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], there are integers $a\leq b$, independent of $n$, for which every $C_n$ is constructible of Tor amplitude $[a,b]$. Testing the definition [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude] with the coefficient module itself gives $\mathcal H^q(C_n)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$. In the tower category [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], kernels and cokernels are formed componentwise: the component transition maps restrict to kernels and descend to quotients. Consequently cohomology is componentwise, and the zero components in degrees $q<a$ make the cohomology tower zero there. Thus $C_\bullet$ belongs to the bounded-below domain of $Rf_{!,\bullet}$.

source.place: The single proof paragraph: finite-level preservation, followed by the uniform interval argument.

proof.text: Write $D_\bullet=Rf_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet$. Apply clause (1) of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] to the supplied compactification and the bounded-below tower from step 1. It gives, for every $n\geq1$, $D_n\simeq Rf_{!,A_n}C_n$, where $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. This is precisely the tower operation in the statement; no levelwise choices or alteration of transition maps are made.

source.place: The single proof paragraph: finite-level preservation, followed by the uniform interval argument.

proof.text: Apply the finite-ring assertion of [det-sp-tower-bound-uniform] to each $C_n$. Its standing geometric hypotheses are exactly those made explicit in the statement; the bound is on the geometric fibres of $f$, not those of its proper compactification. Its coefficient hypotheses hold: [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] gives a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and a unit-power decomposition $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $e\geq1$, since $|\ell|_E<1$. Therefore $A_n=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^{en})$ is one of its finite commutative coefficient rings, and is killed by $\ell^n$. The cited finite-ring assertion gives $Rf_{!,A_n}C_n\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ with Tor interval $[a,b+2d]$. Step 2 identifies this object with $D_n$. Both $d$ and $[a,b]$ are independent of $n$, so this is a common output Tor interval, including all finite-level constructibility assertions.

source.place: The single proof paragraph: finite-level preservation, followed by the uniform interval argument.

proof.text: For each $n$, test the Tor interval of $D_n$ with the degree-zero tensor unit $A_{n,Y}$ in [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. Since $D_n\otimes^L_{A_{n,Y}}A_{n,Y}\simeq D_n$, its cohomology vanishes outside $[a,b+2d]$. The levels are constructible by step 3, have the common Tor interval from that step and now a common cohomological interval. These are exactly all conditions defining $\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ in [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Thus $D_\bullet$ belongs to the stated category. The normalization condition in that definition is separate and is never used.

lean.note: The geometric operations are those of det-sp-tower-shriek-levels, transported by its section-normalized realization equivalence to the original coefficient towers. The level comparison is a natural isomorphism restricted to D+; the preservation clause uses exactly spConstructibleTorTowers, without normalization. The geometric hypothesis explicitly allows smooth pure relative dimension d or the general geometric fibre bound.
